newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes lower in pre-Christmas slowdow.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes lower in pre-Christmas slowdow.

text.p: Trading activity on the Prague Stock Exchange was quieter on Friday with dealers saying institutional investors especially were winding down their operations ahead of the Christmas break.
The PX50 index edged 0.14 percent lower to 516 while the RPIX index of continuously traded shares lost 0.08 percent to 1,061.7.
"The foreigners - nothing has really changed their appetite for the moment. Institutional investors are really cleaning the house ahead of Chrtistmas," said Jan Sykora of Wood & Company.
Echoing the views of many in the market, Sykora said investment funds were attracting increasing attention on rumours that many closed funds were looking to go open ended.
"The only sector looking more interesting is the fund sector where some funds are looking to go open ended," he said.
In recent weeks SPIF Cesky, a closed investment fund, has been bought aggressively after SPIF said that it was searching for a way to go open ended.
On Friday, the fund again dominated continuous trading accounting for around 60 million crowns of the 70 million traded during the session.
SPIF closed up five crowns to 430. RIF investment fund also rose, gaining 10 crowns to 815. On Friday December 20, RIF is due to hold an extraordinary general meeting.
Overall, turnover slipped to 507 million crowns.
